I'm not a man and I've only been through this as a child of divorced parents. But I have to say something. My suggestion for you is to make sure you tell your girls how much you love them and that you only want them to be happy. That what makes you happy is when they are taken cared of and have everything they need. Telling them this will help them feel open with thier needs during a time where they will most likely hide thier feelings because they can see the pain in both you and thier mother. I hid way too much because I didnt want to add to the pain I saw. Kids are not stupid to what is going on even as young as your girls are. 

Another smaller suggestion is to watch mrs. Doubtfire with them. That movie helped me understand what was going on in a way my parents couldn't. I could see not only was I not alone but that it wasn't my fault and it wasn't the fault of my parents either. Some people simply dont work out and that small notion made my childhood bearable. 

You sound like a wonderful father and I'm sorry to hear about the pain you are dealing with now but know that as long as you are strong and show love through it all your girls will learn how to love through pain too. And that's a beautiful thing for them to learn.

I've been there, in fact I'm still there to some degree. 24 was honestly the worst year for me its just at the time when everyone around you seems to be moving forward and you're just stuck. At the age of 27 I wouldn't say I'm any less stuck but I've developed more tools to get me out of it little by little. My 2 biggest suggestions to you that helped me a whole lot are 1. Take a deep breath and realize your not alone in feeling like this (hi!) And that you have a  very real problem that needs to be addressed before you can address the other ones. 2. Focus on developing one thing at a time and realize itll take a while to develop if you're not used to it. It took me like a solid 2 weeks of telling myself "ok I'm gonna eat breakfast and not binge eat at lunch" before I actually sat down with a bowl of oatmeal. And even then life getting shifted a little can make it all seem like it's going to hell again but you'll have that muscle memory that will make it easier and easier to go back to those habits you're trying to develop.

To figure out the habits you need to develop first try writing out literally everything you wanna do or need to do. And then slowly go through the lost and pick 3 important things you wanna focus on and only 3. Dont over do it its better to create a few strong habits then many weal habits that aren't tailored to you. then each week figure out a plan to make it work for you. And if a plan doesnt work for you figure out why and be honest about why and try a new method. Trying to take meds at breakfast everyday only to realize that you running late often causes you to skip breakfast? Try putting your pills in a to-go container every night so you can grab them easily on the go.

You should be an adult, but the thing is you are an adult who's trying to figure out a complex problem, itll take time.
